summary_en.validation: Experimental compression testing validated the mechanical properties, and results were compared with analytical models.

summary_zh.motivation: 解决全髋假体因刚度过大导致的应力遮挡和远期松动问题。
summary_zh.method: 设计金刚石立方晶格多孔股骨柄，利用LPBF制造并进行ISO标准静力学测试。
summary_zh.result: 多孔柄刚度比实心柄降低31%，数字图像相关验证了数值模型。
summary_zh.validation: ISO 7206-4静力学实验结合数字图像相关与数值模型对比。

summary_en.motivation: To mitigate stress shielding and aseptic loosening in total hip arthroplasty by reducing femoral stem stiffness via porous lattice design.
summary_en.method: A diamond cubic lattice femoral stem was designed, fabricated by laser powder bed fusion from Ti-6Al-4V, and tested under static loading per ISO 7206-4.
summary_en.result: The porous stem exhibited a 31% reduction in stiffness compared to its dense counterpart, validated by digital image correlation and numerical modeling.
summary_en.validation: Static mechanical testing with digital image correlation and finite element analysis provided experimental-numerical correlation.

summary_en.motivation: To investigate the effect of implant surface roughness on the mechanical behavior of total hip arthroplasty, particularly at the bone-implant interface.
summary_en.method: Combined experimental mechanical testing and finite element analysis to simulate stress distribution and micromotion under different roughness conditions.
summary_en.result: Surface roughness significantly influences interface stress distribution and micromotion magnitude, suggesting that optimized roughness can enhance implant stability.
summary_en.validation: Experimental mechanical tests validated the finite element model predictions of interface mechanical responses.

summary_en.motivation: To overcome the computational burden and complex setup of patient-specific finite element analysis for time-sensitive clinical applications.
summary_en.method: A deep learning model was developed to directly map FEA inputs to aortic wall stress distributions, bypassing the traditional FEA solver.
summary_en.result: The DL surrogate predicted Von Mises stress distributions with average errors of 0.492% and peak stress errors of 0.891%.
summary_en.validation: Validation was performed by comparing DL predictions against ground-truth FEA results on unseen patient-specific models.
